title: fix: Claude CLI Bash commands disappear from Telegram progress after completion
body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Telegram progress drafts lose a Claude CLI Bash command when its terminal activity item replaces the running row, even with `commandText: "raw"`. ## User Impact User impact: The draft retains native Bash command detail after completion. Ambiguous MCP loopback results still do not assert that the requested command was executed. No configuration change is needed. ## Why This Change Was Made The CLI event producer has the original request arguments, but native tool completion items previously used only loopback executed arguments, which native Bash does not have. The projection now retains original arguments only for native CLI tools while continuing to require authoritative executed arguments for MCP calls, including generic `tool_use` events with MCP-prefixed names. ## Evidence - Merged current main `96a91f0e005ef02d95c3249249839ad6c4df64f8` without rewriting contributor commits. Candidate head: `5950af2de1f352b46c39925176031108c578e5cf`. - Real Telegram **Test Server** proof used the checkout's userbot runner, Convex-leased bot/user credentials, isolated fresh Gateway builds, and a fake `claude` executable emitting native Bash start/completion and generic MCP-prefixed tool events. No Claude service or paid provider was used. The baseline was the merged checkout with its sole production diff reverted to the byte-identical pinned-main event owner, built separately in the same worktree. - **Before:** the same Telegram draft changed from `Bash print text, echo P158636_NATIVE_RETAINED running` to `Bash` when the native call completed. **After:** its completed row retained `Bash print text, echo P158636_NATIVE_RETAINED`. - **Controls on both builds:** the still-running Bash row retained `echo P158636_STILL_RUNNING`; after the ambiguous MCP result, its row became `Exec` without `echo P158636_UNCONFIRMED`. Each run observed six draft edits and one separate final reply. TDLib message/edit readback and the real Telegram Web screenshots below supply the before/after evidence. - All six run-owned QA messages were deleted and checked absent with TDLib `getMessages` under their respective leases. Both runners completed with credential scratch removed and leases released. Telegram Web capture was subsequently completed under one Convex lease and one Web K Test Server login; see the paired screenshots below. - The regression failed against the pinned-main owner for the intended reason: completed Bash metadata lacked `echo retained`. It passed on the candidate, including three ambiguous MCP event/name variants. `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.command-progress.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **22.741 s wall**, Vitest 19.66 s including worker-artifact preparation. Final-head CI measured this test at **0.070 s (70 ms)** in [checks-node-changed-compact-large-31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36447083807/job/109013413516); that job passed. This is test execution time, separate from local cold-start wall time. - Production and core test types passed after correcting the test fixture's tuple inference. Touched-file type-aware lint and formatting passed. Both fresh `pnpm build` invocations completed; their logs also reported an unrelated Control UI gzip-budget warning (the fresh hosted Control UI performance job passed). - **Maintainer intent:** inspected Pash's `a2bbcbf40684` (Keep connected apps usable and Slack previews quiet). This diff leaves authored-preamble `phase: "end"` unchanged. No Slack QA Lab scenario covered this preview configuration, so focused Slack dispatch/projection tests were used: six cases passed, covering hidden tool rows with `toolProgress: false`, `label: false`, quiet intermediate failures, and complete-preamble retention for default/compact style. This is projection proof, not a live Slack claim. ### Refreshed validation Merged current main `026348d107c729ac905d8075114f582336d4bfd1` preserving all contributor commits; candidate head `be979ccae777addf9b69d382199ed1352ea46f74`. The native event owner is unchanged by the merge. Rebuilt the Gateway and repeated the real Telegram Test Server run after the draft-owner updates: completed Bash command retained, still-running row unchanged, ambiguous MCP row without unconfirmed command. All three new QA messages were deleted and read back absent; the lease and scratch were released. The existing before/after screenshots remain representative. The focused regression and all 201 Slack draft-dispatch tests passed with one worker (regression shard 40.87 s including cold worker-artifact preparation; full Slack file 37.53 s). Core production and core test types passed, as did touched-file formatting and type-aware lint. Watching one fresh CI run and the hosted exact-head review; the older unrelated watcher-ready failure is prior-head evidence only. ### Contributor's earlier production-bot screenshots These are supplementary production-bot images, not the Test Server evidence above. ### Telegram Test Server: paired live progress screenshots Both captures use one leased QA user, one browser login, the same fake Claude CLI event sequence, and `commandText: "raw"`. The main-owner build loses the completed first Bash command; the candidate retains it. The second Bash row is still running and unchanged, and the completed ambiguous MCP row shows only `Exec`. Crops exclude the chat list, header, usernames and chat identifiers. After capture, all six messages from this paired run were deleted and verified absent, the exact browser session was terminated and checked absent, and the runner released its lease and removed credential scratch. ![Before: completed native Bash command detail disappears on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7b622c9-f609-45a7-8efc-ee3fed821aa7) ![After: completed native Bash command detail remains on the candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/374e0e49-31f0-4066-b69f-cc60e7e59223) ### Third-party MCP correction Head `9305048adc77f0fb9b707da3aebe26c7fdbe93fc` also excludes generic third-party `mcp_` names from the native-only fallback. The new `mcp_docs_exec` regression failed before the correction because terminal metadata contained `requested command`, then passed after the correction. The simpler predicate replaces the redundant source/OpenClaw-only checks without changing diagnostic or preamble behavior. A fresh built Gateway and Convex-leased Telegram Test Server turn confirmed completed native Bash command retention, the unchanged still-running Bash row, and a terminal `Mcp Docs Exec` row with no unconfirmed requested command. All three QA messages were deleted and read back absent, then credential scratch and the lease were released. The focused test passed in **21.502 s single-worker wall time**, with 18 ms test execution (Vitest 18.79 s including cold worker preparation). Touched-file formatting/type-aware lint and the affected agents-other test-type graph passed. The existing paired screenshots and full 201-case Slack projection proof remain valid. ### Final quiet-operation preservation Head `5c398918128608d87bae140da71968fc9d787ab3` preserves the existing quiet `process.poll` behavior without restoring unconfirmed command metadata: request arguments are used only by the existing activity visibility projection when execution arguments are absent. This repairs the sibling test failure at `execute-events.tool-result-args.test.ts:237`; the two focused files now pass **42 tests**. No public API, configuration, defaults, or preamble-boundary changes were introduced. A fresh built-Gateway Telegram Test Server run retained native Bash detail, omitted the completed third-party MCP command, and kept completed process polling silent. Its three messages were deleted and read back absent before lease release. Touched-file type-aware lint and formatting and the fresh build passed. ### Final-head CI evidence Hosted review is **ready** on `5c398918128608d87bae140da71968fc9d787ab3`. [Fresh CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36447083807) completed with all agent test shards and static checks green. Remaining failures are outside this two-file CLI-event diff and exercise mocked-Gateway UI behavior, not the Claude CLI: - `checks-ui-e2e (2/9)`: `chat-motion.e2e.test.ts`, `finishSendMotion:81`, expected 2 to be greater than 2. [Same assertion on another PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36437889732/job/108982451192), SHA `42e2780bb8ef6abbd4bc9ad6aa9b4506e0338ca2`. - `checks-ui-e2e (7/9)`: `chat-session-companion-focus.e2e.test.ts`, `preserves newer input intent while a side answer is pending: cleared draft`, request-observation timeout at `control-ui-e2e-controls.ts:223`. [Same file/helper timeout on another PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36438074545/job/108983035018), SHA `aef4362eab057b88f494ca6e294a9b14feeb2fef`, but a different focus scenario; this is not claimed as an exact-case reproduction. - `openclaw/ci-gate` reports the two UI shard failures above. No failing CI job was rerun.
